question: Croatia became a member of the EU in 2013. 1.
What benefits has the European common market brought for the Croatian economy?
What damage has the European common market done to the Croatian economy?
answer: 1. The European Single Market has brought important benefits to the Croatian economy. Firstly, the access to the Single Market has enabled Croatian businesses to trade with businesses from other Member States without facing tariffs or barriers to trade, leading to increased exports and imports and economic growth.

Secondly, the integration in the EU has made Croatia a more attractive destination for foreign investors due to the stability and predictability of its regulatory environment. This has facilitated greater foreign direct investment inflows, contributing to economic development.

The main investing countries are all members of the EU: the Netherlands (16%), Austria (14%), Germany (11%), Luxembourg (10%), Italy (9%), and Hungary (7%). Lastly, integration into the Single Market has encouraged Croatia to make structural reforms, including the improvement of its business environment, and align its regulations and standards with those of the EU.

This process of convergence has increased competitiveness and efficiency of Croatian businesses. Those benefits of the Single Market add to the other benefits of being a member of the EU, notably the access to EU funds, including EUR 9 billion from Cohesion Policy in 2021-2027, EUR 10 billion from the Recovery and Resilience Facility (EUR 5.8 billion in grants and EUR 4.

2 billion in favourable loans) and access to the Technical Support Instrument that has supported Croatia through more than 100 project design and implement reforms in many policy areas. 2. The European Single Market has not damaged the Croatian economy, but its positive impact has varied across sectors and regions.
Structural funds aim at helping all regions and the whole Croatian population to reap the benefits of the Single Market.
